title: GPU Pool Insights & Burst Tuner — Dedicated Capacity dashboard redesign
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Design a consolidated GPU Pool Insights panel and an inline Burst Tuner control for Redwood Dedicated capacity. The goal is to help platform and SRE users quickly assess pool health, understand autoscale behavior, preview cost implications of burst settings, and safely apply temporary burst capacity without surprising downstream apps. Deliver high-fidelity prototypes, annotated specs for engineering, accessibility checks, and a short usability test with two platform teams.
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity Figma screens for Pool Overview, Pool Detail, and Burst Tuner modal/component
Annotated component spec covering metrics, data latency expectations, and interactive states
Cost-preview slider that computes delta cost and estimated throughput change in real-time (mock calculation acceptable)
Autoscale policy editor with inline validation and suggested defaults based on historical utilization
Design sign-off from PM (Jasmine Li) and Eng leads (Sanjay Rao) with noted engineering concerns resolved in spec
Accessibility audit: color contrast >= 4.5:1, keyboard operable controls, and screen-reader labels for all interactive elements
design_notes: Primary view includes: temporal heatmap of GPU utilization (hourly), 95th/50th latency bands, current active pods, queued requests, and shortest time-to-scale estimate
Burst Tuner lives as an inline control on Pool Detail and as a fallback modal for bulk edits. It exposes: burst cap (GPUs), duration, cooldown, and cost-preview slider
Cost-preview uses three tiers: conservative/expected/aggressive and shows estimated $/hour and estimates of tokens/sec improvement
Include small explainer component for 'burst credits' concept and audit trail link to console activity log
Heatmap uses pattern fill + color to remain accessible for colorblind users; we add separate numeric overlays on hover/focus
decisions: Use temporal heatmap instead of stacked area chart to surface hotspots and intermittent saturation events
Expose burst as a time-bounded override rather than permanent setting to reduce accidental cost exposure
Preview cost calculations are conservative by default and include a clear CTA to view detailed cost report in Billing
Autoscale editor will suggest a default policy computed from last 7 days of median utilization; engineering owns the baseline calculation but design defines UI hooks and validation messages
review_comments: PM Jasmine Li: Add explicit 'estimated cost impact' callout when burst > 2 GPUs — product wants an extra confirmation step
Eng Sanjay Rao: Need clarifying spec on margin of error for throughput estimates; will coordinate with backend to return confidence bands
Design lead Marco Diaz: Move burst toggle closer to autoscale policy summary and surface historical burst usage in the modal
Accessibility review (Nina Patel): Ensure heatmap has texture/pattern fallback and colorblind-safe palette; also add ARIA live regions for async updates

next_steps: Incorporate PM and Eng feedback: add confirm modal for large burst sizes and surface confidence bands in throughput estimates
Finalize annotated spec and component list for engineering handoff (target 2025-03-24)
Run two 30-minute moderated sessions with platform SREs and consolidate usability notes (UX researcher: Priya Das)
Coordinate with telemetry team to publish sample queries and expected metric TTLs
Create a lightweight A/B experiment plan to validate cost-preview comprehension before GA
stakeholders: Sanjay Rao — Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime
ux_considerations: Keep burst control reversible and clearly time-bounded to avoid surprise billing
Provide multiple data densities: compact list for quick triage and expanded view for deep-dive
Use progressive disclosure: show critical signals upfront and hide advanced policy tuning behind an 'Advanced' section
Keyboard-first interactions on heatmap and policy editor; ensure focus visible and persisted state for form errors
telemetry_requirements: Latency of metrics: UI can tolerate up to 30s data lag; annotate UI where older data is shown
Expose: per-pool GPU utilization (1m, 5m), queue length, active pods, model routing counts, recent burst events
Backend should return a 95% confidence band for throughput predictions or a metadata flag if unavailable
Audit events for burst changes must include actor, reason, duration, and pre/post pool state for console activity log
